summary: Initial cold codegen for chemical_detector: 19 files, two controllers (GasAnalysisController, MovementController) plus a ChemicalDetector driver. All 81 requirements are traced in result_codegen.json. The flagged items are design choices and invented defaults; none is known to block the pipeline.

issues.title: Gas-analysis 'final state' realised as SOURCE_FOUND -> CONCLUDED (no Final mode)
issues.raw: CD-GA-Beh6 ends gas analysis in a final state after emitting stop. This controller is the one whose Isabelle theory is generated (CLAUDE.md: no Final mode allowed), and every mode needs an outgoing transition. A self-loop on the state entered with `stop` would re-run its lifted entry and re-send stop on every loop, so a two-step terminal is used: GAS_DETECTED -[ins>=thr]/stop-> SOURCE_FOUND -> CONCLUDED. CONCLUDED absorbs further gas readings (storing gs, per CD-GA-Var1) without classifying them, so no further turn/stop/resume is ever emitted.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm that an idle, gas-absorbing CONCLUDED state is an acceptable reading of 'concludes its search, processing no further readings'.

issues.title: Movement Found -> HALTED terminal with a stop-triggered self-loop
issues.raw: CD-MV-Beh9 (Found_to_Final). FOUND emits flag and halts on entry, then moves autonomously to HALTED. HALTED keeps a stop-triggered self-loop, so it has an outgoing transition without re-running Found's entry (a single flag).
issues.fix_directive: Confirm HALTED + stop self-loop as the realisation of 'Once in Found the movement subsystem stays halted'.

issues.title: Constant values are not given by the requirements
issues.raw: thr=3.0, lv=1.0, evadeTime=1, stuckPeriod=3, stuckDist=1.0, outPeriod=2 (integer-valued, small, to keep the CSP model finite and small). The requirements say these are 'configured at system startup' without giving values.
issues.fix_directive: Replace with deployment values if known.

issues.title: Meaning of 'indicates the target chemical', target identity, and empty-reading defaults
issues.raw: analysis returns gasD iff some sensor reports the configured target Chem (by id, passed to GasFunctions) with intensity > 0. intensity/location return 0.0/Front on an empty reading (their stated precondition is non-empty); location breaks ties towards the lowest position.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm the classification criterion and tie-breaking.

issues.title: Sensor position to Angle mapping (angle(x))
issues.raw: CD-Fn3 uses angle(x) but does not define it. Positions cycle Front, Right, Back, Left (1->Front, 2->Right, 3->Back, 4->Left, 5->Front, ...).
issues.fix_directive: Replace with the real sensor-array geometry.

issues.title: intensity() is the peak over all sensors, not only the target chemical
issues.raw: CD-Fn2 defines intensity as the maximum i over the whole sequence, while analysis is about the target chemical only. Implemented literally (all sensors), so a strong non-target reading can drive the threshold check and the turn direction.
issues.fix_directive: Confirm whether intensity/location should be restricted to the target chemical.

issues.title: Threshold guard written as `ins >= THR`, not a goreq(...) call
issues.raw: CD-Fn4 says the threshold check uses goreq. A guard predicate whose initialiser is a bare method call becomes an unconstrained boolean in the extracted model, so it would lose the link to ins/thr. The guard uses the primitive comparison, which is exactly goreq's definition. goreq itself is implemented and used by intensity/location.
issues.fix_directive: None unless the model must literally reference goreq.

issues.title: Second outgoing branch of Analysis / AvoidingAgain written as `else`
issues.raw: Analysis: `sts == noGas` -> NO_GAS, else -> GAS_DETECTED (equivalent to sts == gasD because Status has exactly two values). AvoidingAgain: progress -> AVOIDING, else -> GETTING_OUT (the requirement's stuck condition is exactly the negation of progress). The else form makes the guard pair an explicit P / not P total cover.

issues.title: Waiting's during-action randomWalk() and the wait() actions
issues.raw: randomWalk() is called at the head of the WAITING block on every cycle (during semantics in Java; the extractor records it as Waiting's entry). wait(evadeTime)/wait(outPeriod) are Vehicle.pause(n) requests: the step() method never blocks.

issues.title: Operations are Vehicle methods / a ChangeDirection class, not compute() classes
issues.raw: move, randomWalk and shortRandomWalk are platform operations (CD-OP1..3 say 'provided by the Vehicle') and have no computed result, so they are Vehicle methods. changeDirection(l) (CD-OP4) has conditional behaviour, which a compute() body (assignments only) cannot express, so it is a ChangeDirection class calling Vehicle.move. The extractor emits move as an operation call and changeDirection as an output event.
issues.fix_directive: None unless compute()-style operation classes are mandatory.

issues.title: A turn arriving while in AvoidingAgain is dropped by the Java
issues.raw: AvoidingAgain has no turn transition. In the model the sender blocks until AvoidingAgain is left, which happens autonomously on the next cycle. In the Java step model, a turn delivered in that cycle is consumed without updating `a`, and the next gas reading re-issues a turn.
issues.fix_directive: Decide whether AvoidingAgain should record `a` on turn.

issues.title: Chem modelled as record Chem(int id)
issues.raw: Chem is an opaque identity with equality only; a single-nat record gives value equality without inventing chemical names.

next_step: Run the pipeline (compile -> coverage -> preflight -> t2m -> m2m -> m2t -> verifiers).
